findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch (symbol R1, uuid c5c38e1a-7593-5c99-b971-2f9d2e7bef78, line 1261 '(dnp yes)') and inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb (footprint R1, uuid 8404a180-a151-464e-8f25-8cf316cdcba5, line 304 '(attr smd dnp)')
findings.mechanism: R1 (10k, R_0805) is the only element whose terminals bridge nets /IN and /OUT (netlist: /IN = {J1.1, R1.1}, /OUT = {C1.1, J1.2, R1.2}). It is marked do-not-populate in both the schematic and the board, consistently. All board copper is single-net (the saved board passed DRC with 0 clearance violations and 0 unconnected items, so copper cannot bridge nets), and the only other fitted two-terminal part, C1 (100n), sits between /OUT and GND and is a DC open. With R1 absent, net /IN consists solely of J1 pin 1, one 4.09 mm track, and the orphaned R1 pad 1 — a floating stub with no DC continuity to /OUT. An ngspice operating point on the saved population confirms 1 V applied at /IN produces 0 V and 0 A at /OUT (a fitted 10k would produce ≈90.9 mV into the 1 k sense load).
findings.reasoning: This is the exact failure mode the scope singles out: the unpopulated R1 footprint is the only conceivable /IN-to-/OUT conductor and may not be assumed to conduct. Both native authorities (schematic dnp flag and board footprint dnp attribute) agree R1 is not fitted, and no alternate assembly override exists per the scope. The connectivity reconstruction and the SPICE demonstration independently show the saved assembly leaves /IN electrically floating relative to /OUT, so the single stated acceptance criterion is violated. Severity is blocking because the requirement cannot be met by the saved population under any stated operating condition.
findings.title: R1 is DNP in the saved assembly: no fitted resistive DC path connects /IN to /OUT

findings.mechanism: KiCad ERC and DRC validate design-level connectivity and geometry in which a DNP footprint still owns its pads and nets; neither tool has a rule that a DNP part breaks electrical continuity, and no DNP-related check exists in either report's rule set (the ignored-check lists cover unrelated rules such as single_global_label and missing_courtyard). A successful tool exit and zero violations therefore say nothing about whether the fitted population conducts.
findings.reasoning: Recorded so the clean check outcomes in this packet are not read as evidence against CIRC-01. This is a verification-coverage observation about what the native tools measure, not a tool failure: both runs executed correctly on the saved files.
findings.title: Passing ERC/DRC/parity checks do not verify the assembly-population criterion

findings.mechanism: An assembler working from BOM/centroid outputs that include R1 could fit the part contrary to the saved DNP population, or conversely be left to resolve the contradiction manually; the authoritative saved population (DNP) is only visible via the dnp flags.
findings.reasoning: Under the stated scope the saved population (R1 not fitted) governs, and this review evaluates that population (CIRC-01). The mixed flags do not change the saved assembly but are an ambiguity hazard in generated manufacturing outputs; flagged as a minor concern rather than a defect because KiCad BOM tooling can filter on the DNP attribute and no explicit documentation requirement was stated.
findings.title: R1 population metadata is internally inconsistent: DNP yet still in BOM and placement files

limitations: SPICE check used ideal elements; adequate here because the criterion is topological (presence of any fitted resistive DC path), not parametric.
Zone fill evaluated as saved (candidate is read-only, no refill pass); the single zone is on GND and cannot affect /IN-/OUT connectivity in any fill state.

No component rating, derating, thermal, or qualification review performed: the stated requirements explicitly exclude unstated ratings, and no operating conditions beyond the DC-path criterion were given.
No AC/transfer-function verification of the RC filter was performed; the packet states only the fitted resistive DC path criterion.
J1 mating connector/harness behavior not assessed (nothing stated); no assumption of external bridging was made.
